title: Power Rankings: Heat hold off Bulls for No. 1 spot
heading: 2011-12 Power Rankings: Week 2
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: It's been only eight games, but the best start to a season in LeBron's career should leave little doubt as to why so many of us have been bangin' on him to force himself to operate closer to the bucket: He's shooting a ridiculous 60.1 percent from the floor.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's the Bulls' best start since MJ's 1996-97 team went 8-0. And if it's possible, Chicago's D -- particularly the bigs -- looks even more imposing than it did last season if you throw out Saturday's egg in Atlanta, with four of its last five foes held under 85 points.

rankings.summaryHtml: Six teams have had a back-to-back-to-back set already, and all six, bizarrely, won the third game after teams went 28-36 in that situation during Lockout 1999. Only OKC, though, went a perfect 3-0 ... despite losing Eric Maynor for the season in the middle of it.

rankings.summaryHtml: Question: Why is Danny Granger, who's averaged at least 19.6 ppg since 2007-08, down to 14.9 ppg? Answer: These Pacers, who just rode their newfound balance to a nice little win in Boston, have a whopping seven players scoring in double figures.

rankings.summaryHtml: Dwight Howard was probably due for the sort of foul-trouble nightmare he endured in Sunday's stroll past Sacramento. In the season's first five games, by contrast, Dwight racked up only 13 fouls. Better yet: DH12's been hit with only one T in nine games.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Celts will dive into a testing stretch -- Dallas, Chicago and OKC at home with a quick trip to Indy thrown in -- with plenty of rest, given that they haven't played since Friday. If only Friday's outing wasn't a momentum-sapping loss at home to the Pacers.

rankings.summaryHtml: Thanks to a wicked early schedule, Houston is 0-5 on the road, which is the Rockets' worst road start since an 0-7 opening in 1982-83. Which they could probably tolerate if they knew, like in '82-83, they'd be getting the No. 1 overall pick in the draft.
